newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY AND AVALANCHE BURY COYOTES 6-0.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY AND AVALANCHE BURY COYOTES 6-0.

text.p: Patrick Roy made 20 saves for his league-leading fourth shutout of the season and Jon Klemm scored twice for his first career multi-goal game as the Colorado Avalanche routed the Phoenix Coyotes 6-0 Wednesday.

Roy was hardly tested, stopping seven shots in the first and second periods and six in the third en route to his his 34th career shutout. He is 9-0-2 in his last 11 games and leads the league with 13 victories.
"Roy was effective because he was able to see the first shot," Coyotes coach Don Hay said. "He can save everything he can see."
Sandis Ozolinsh had two goals and an assist for the Avalanche, who improved to 5-0-2 in their last seven home games. Colorado is a league-best 14-5-4 for 32 points.
Joe Sakic and Mike Keane had the other goals for the defending Stanley Cup champions.
Phoenix, playing its first road game since November 1, dropped to 1-4-2 in its last seven games.

In Calgary, Roman Turek made his NHL debut a victorious one by stopping 24 shots and Brent Gilchrist added a pair of goals as the Dallas Stars concluded a successful three-game road trip with a 3-1 victory over the Flames.

The 26-year-old Turek led the Czech Republic to the World Championship last May, playing every minute of all eight games and posting a stellar 1.88 goals-against average. He did not make the Stars out of training camp, but was recalled to back up starter Andy Moog.
Pat Verbeek scored the other Dallas goal as the Stars concluded their road trip with a pair of victories and are 4-1-1 in their last six overall.
Calgary goaltender Trevor Kidd stopped 25 shots, but fell to 7-6-1. Dave Gagner had the lone Flames tally.
At Florida, John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 27 shots, including all 15 in the final period, and Scott Mellanby had a goal and an assist as the Panthers beat the Los Angeles Kings 4-1.
Vanbiesbrouck wasn't tested through much of the first period but was strong over the final 40 minutes, turning aside 24-of-25 shots in improving to 9-2-3 on the season.
Brian Skrudland, Dave Lowry and Jody Hull had the other Florida goals. Ray Ferraro tallied for the Kings.

In Hartford, Paul Coffey snapped a tie with a power-play goal 3:40 into the third period and Sean Burke made 34 saves to help the Whalers extend their best-ever start with a 3-1 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.

Andrew Cassels and Sami Kapanen also scored and Geoff Sanderson added two assists for Hartford, which is 4-0-1 in its last five games. The Whalers, who improved to 7-2-1 at home, lead the Northeast Division with 23 points.
Hartford's 10-5-3 start after 18 games is its best since joining the NHL in 1979.
Stephane Richer scored for Montreal.

In Anaheim, newly acquired Bryan Smolinksi scored his first goal of the season 6:32 into the second period and Tommy Salo and Guy Hebert had a goaltending duel as the New York Islanders played to a 2-2 tie with the Mighty Ducks.
Each team had countless chances to win the game in both overtime and the third period, but Salo and Hebert were equal to the task. Salo had 27 saves for the Isles and Hebert 29 for Anaheim.
Smolinski, acquired from Pittsburgh on Sunday, made his Islander debut after spending the first part of the season with Detroit of the International Hockey League.
Claude Lapointe also tallied for the Islanders, 1-3-3 in their last seven games. They have a league-leading seven ties.
Kevin Todd and Teemu Selanne had goals for Anaheim, which is an NHL-worst 4-13-3.
